steps.content: The cyan silhouettes multiply as you press on, packed ever tighter, yet none acknowledge you. They simply cycle through the same ritual: kneel, pray, bow.
You and Chengxiao move through them with practiced discipline, adhering to the safest rule: don't look, don't listen, don't ask. Shut them out as completely as you can.
As you walk past, one of the phantoms suddenly leans in close.
Its outline sags before you, loose and shapeless, the shoulders and arms pleated with deep folds that look ready to slump into nothing.

steps.speaker: Phantom
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>...Could you... hear me...

steps.speaker: Phantom
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>...Could you... tell them... I'm still waiting... I can keep waiting...

steps.speaker: Phantom
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>...Please... let our wish be granted...
<color=#fb9259>Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits.</color>
The figure bows low before you, a deep and solemn kowtow, and then it is gone. But the sound of its weeping remains, soaking slowly into your thoughts like water through cloth.

steps.speaker: Faint Voice
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>Mom... does it still hurt...? Why do I keep dreaming you're hurting...? Just like that day... you curled up so small...

steps.speaker: Faint Voice
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>Let me see you one last time... come tell me yourself... please...?

steps.speaker: Faint Voice
steps.content: <i><color=#7683a2>Just one last time...
You don't know these people, or the ones they mourn. But the weight inside their voices, that you know intimately.
The desperate begging, the wailing, the prayers born from hopelessness: you've seen and heard them all before. And yet, is there really nothing you can do...?
A thick, wet footfall sounds at your ear, and Chengxiao steps up beside you.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: It would seem these are souls who perished in a fire. The Eastern Continent has seen several major fires in recent years. The largest among them claimed hundreds of thousands of lives in a single night.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Were you... there?

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: That one, I did foresee.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then did you try to do anything? Before it happened?

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: I contacted the local authorities. They dismissed it as baseless nonsense. "Your reputation lies in ruins," they said, "and now you stoop to spreading rumors..."
Chengxiao lifts his palm toward the floating green specks. They orbit his arm in a few slow loops, then veer off into the distance.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: But the "rumors" spread all the same. The people panicked, and so the authorities sealed the city. When the fire came, no one could get out.
The note of weariness in his words vanishes like the scattered green sparks, replaced by his usual cool composure.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: So you see, prophecy is a thing that cuts both ways. Believe it or not, the outcome is no different. The old saying goes that the will of heaven must never be revealed—not because revealing it invites divine punishment, but because revealing it changes nothing. The fate has already been written.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Do you believe in it, then? Prophecy.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Lichen told me your shifu came to you both in a dream, said you'd find a "god" here. Is that why you're here in Maria City?

steps.speaker: No, no. I don't care about the truth or falsehood of gods or games. Those are from the work. I've seen all sorts of absurd things at work. Plus, you've paid me well.
steps.content: I believe in the fate that prophecy reveals. But what concerns me more is causality. Everything that happens has its reasons.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: I want to know what has been sending us these dreams, and why.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But if you believe fate is already set, what's the point of knowing the process? Is it just academic curiosity?

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Fate may be beyond changing. But the process can still offer insight. Should something similar come to pass again, at least one would know what to expect.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But what if one day, something you learn from the process turns out to be exactly what you need to change something?

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Then I would call it a welcome surprise. But that is not why I came.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: The laws of causality exist for a reason. Wanting to change everything, that is Li Xianling's way. She can scorn the price for breaking those laws all she likes. The price will find her regardless.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: You have seen it yourself. Those who attempt to cross the boundary between life and death become nothing more than these wandering phantoms in the Void of Yin, trapped in endless suffering. She is already well down that road.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: What, do you think I'm a rather poor excuse for an uncle?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...No. You're right. I've lived through everything you said myself.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I'm still curious. You foresee it all, and you can't change a thing. Can you really live with that? Like with that fire.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Are you asking because you want to know if I can live with it? Or because you cannot?

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: Then what is it you wish to change?
Your lips part, but you find yourself staring at his face with nothing to say. No answer has formed. You simply cannot bring yourself to speak.
While the silence drags on, several pale green shadows begin to drift toward him.
Chengxiao lifts a finger to his lips, hushing you. Then he opens his arms wide, as if welcoming them.
That's right: just don't interact. Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits. Follow the rules and nothing will go wrong.
So you do nothing. You only watch as the ghosts gather around him and hold him close. He stands among them as he truly is in death, silent and still.
After a while, the phantoms scatter. Chengxiao smiles.

steps.speaker: Chengxiao
steps.content: See? Everything will be fine.
You want to answer him, to pull your lips into a smile, because you're supposed to feel at ease.
But the gesture won't come. So you turn your face aside instead and look up toward the distant path the phantoms took.
[Altar Background]
It's an ocean of cyan lanterns, stretching endlessly, bathing everything in a light that feels more like a warning than a welcome.
